blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
The British use please, sorry and thank you more than almost any other nation. A British person might say sorry twenty times a day. They say it when they bump into someone, when they ask a question, and even when someone else bumps into them.

It sounds strange at first, but there is a logic. These small words are little "social oils". They make everyday life feel smoother. They show respect without making a fuss.

So learn these three words. Use them a lot. If you do, you will already feel more British.

items.q: How often might a British person say "sorry" in one day?
items.why: "A British person might say sorry twenty times a day."

items.q: The text calls please, sorry and thank you…
items.why: "These small words are little 'social oils'."

items.q: What do these words show?
items.why: "They show respect without making a fuss."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with this idea:
options: Saying sorry too much is a mistake in Britain.
Using please is a good habit.
Saying sorry is normal in Britain.
These small words help everyday life.
items.why: Inferência: o texto pede para usar as palavras bastante, então não vê o excesso como erro.

items.q: The text suggests that saying sorry when someone bumps into YOU is…
items.why: Inferência: o texto cita isso como exemplo natural do costume britânico, não como culpa real.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte falando com um novo colega. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi! Welcome to the team. Can I give you one small tip about working here in the UK?

You will hear the word "sorry" a lot. Do not worry. Most of the time it does not mean you did something wrong. It is just polite. If you walk near someone, you say "sorry". If you want to ask a question, you start with "sorry". It is a social thing, not a big problem.

Please use "please" and "thank you" all the time. You really cannot use them too much here. When you ask me for something, try "could you" or "would you mind". For example: "Could you send me the file?" or "Would you mind helping me?" Both sound very polite.

One last thing. If you drop the word "please", it can sound a little rude, even when you do not mean it. So keep it in. It is a very easy habit, and people will respect you for it. You will feel more British very soon!
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Charlotte say about the word "sorry"?
options: It usually does not mean you did something wrong
It always means a big problem
items.why: "Most of the time it does not mean you did something wrong. It is just polite."

items.q: How often should the colleague use "please" and "thank you"?
items.why: "Please use 'please' and 'thank you' all the time."

items.q: Which two forms does Charlotte give for polite requests?
items.why: "try 'could you' or 'would you mind'."

items.q: Why does Charlotte give this tip on the first day?
options: Because she wants the new colleague to fit in fast
Because it is a company rule with a fine
Because the colleague made a mistake
items.why: Inferência: ela é acolhedora e quer ajudar o colega a se adaptar, não corrigir um erro.

items.q: What does Charlotte suggest about dropping "please"?
options: It saves time and sounds friendly
It can sound rude, even if you do not mean it
items.why: "If you drop the word 'please', it can sound a little rude, even when you do not mean it."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "She is very polite with everyone." Polite means…
items.why: Polite = educado, com boas maneiras.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Can you help me, ___?"
items.why: Please = por favor, usado no pedido educado.

items.q: "He wants to apologise for the mistake." To apologise means to…
items.why: To apologise = pedir desculpas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Good ___ are important at work: we say please and thank you."
items.why: Manners = boas maneiras.

items.q: "We use these words in everyday life." Everyday means…
items.why: Everyday = cotidiano, do dia a dia.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e pedidos educados que aparecem no trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Could you send me the report?" This is…
items.why: Could you… = forma educada de pedir algo.

items.q: "Would you mind closing the door?" This means…
options: Is it a problem for you to close the door? (polite)
items.why: Would you mind + -ing = pedido educado e um pouco mais formal.

items.q: "Thank you for your help." You use this to…
items.why: Thank you = obrigado, para agradecer.

items.q: "Sorry to bother you, but can I ask a question?" This is a polite way to…
options: start a question without being rude
items.why: Sorry to bother you = jeito educado de interromper para pedir algo.

items.q: "Being polite can help you fit in at work." To fit in means to…
items.why: Fit in = se enturmar, se sentir parte do grupo.
